detail: torch defaults torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction (and the fp16 one) to True. Flipping it moves native logits by up to 0.19; the first differing port is L0.o (the attention value mix). The flags are not in saturn_pub numeric_scope, so two runs under different flags share a fingerprint scope, and every number labelled `bound` (explain head bound, forecast _affine/_scores, reads value_mix/head_write, circuits matmul bound) assumes float32 accumulation, which is false under the default. Measured worst |eta|/bound for value_mix is 0.996: inside, with no margin.
evidence: mrun job-bcfca7e0c4ef (flag True vs False), job-c2de4323f91b (first differing port); Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16 cuda eager, beast RTX 4080, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.13.1
next: Owner decision: record both flags in numeric_scope (changes every cut fingerprint; shared saturn_pub) and have bounds refuse or widen when a flag is True.
resolution: fixed 2026-11-13: both CUDA reduced-precision flags are in the numeric scope (saturn_pub/numerics.py); a cut refuses under a different flag and names the field; matmul bounds state their accumulation premise and are refused when it fails (analysis/accumulation.py). Real model: job-5e7d47663d29, job-2db9ca10cabc.

detail: Every trail mark holds a private clone of the full state on the device: 28,672 bytes per token row per mark at the real model's size, L+4 marks per row, retain_rows=None by default. About 80% of a mark's bytes repeat the previous mark (measured on tiny models: 79.5% qwen2 bf16, 79.8% qwen3 fp32). Generating 50 rows from 100 tokens would hold about 5.7 GB of GPU memory (formula, not measured).
evidence: scratch fix-substrate/trail_bytes.py; audit item 7
next: Share unchanged per-layer tensors between consecutive cuts: the decoder cache keeps per-layer tensors, advance gets a never-writes-its-input contract (hooks and ports included), StateCut stops cloning sealed tensors, isolation tests. Or set a finite default retain_rows and rely on recipe replay for far rewinds.
resolution: fixed 2026-11-13: cuts share unchanged tensors; a mark costs what its step wrote. Tiny qwen2 bf16, 32 generated rows: held 392,128 -> 12,032 bytes, per mark 1,743 -> 54; qwen3 fp32 1,427,072 -> 41,344. In-place writes to a sealed cut are detected and refused. Receipts capped at 64; edit tensors and port caches released. Real-model memory not re-measured.

detail: whatif and reads verdicts end `unresolved` on the real model: the propagated rounding bound is not finite after a few layers (interval arithmetic through softmax and SwiGLU). Example: whatif L20.m = 0 scale -> exact 0.424, native 0.4375, `bound unresolved (the propagated bound is not finite)`; reads: `unresolved (changed, but no rounding bound to compare with)`. On tiny bf16 models the bound resolves but is vacuous (38.06 against an effect of 0.0046). So no causal verdict is ever `resolved` at scale.
evidence: mrun job-2c1cebccd74d, job-c37ca590539d; tests/repl_golden/cells_cross_run.out; Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16 cuda eager, beast RTX 4080, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.13.1

resolution: fixed 2026-11-13: verdicts no longer depend on a worst-case rounding bound (none exists in the proofs, and one chain alone is not finite). Rule (analysis/verdict.py, P20): native change = exact float64 change + measured residual; floor = max(|residual|, 2 x dtype spacing at the consumer's logits). detail: mdb cannot yet be pointed at mrun's native runtime (QStore + paged kernels): attach() refuses anything that is not a Hugging Face module tree, and the analysis verbs read weights from HF modules. It is feasible, measured two ways. (1) Tiny Qwen2 fp32 on CPU, lossless FP32 QStore: a proxy around the store (the kernel's only weight seam: embed_rows and matmul(name, x)) leaves paged_forward_kv bitwise unchanged, stops at any of the 43 seam points and re-enters bitwise, and gives 16 ports (h a q k v qr s p A o r n g u f m) bitwise equal to mdb's engine on Hugging Face, logits included; zeroing one MLP neuron changes the logits by the same bits in both. (2) Qwen2.5-1.5B, int8 QStore, CUDA: decode token 11.9 ms, 11.8 ms through an inert proxy, 12.7 ms capturing all seam values (393 seam calls); reaching a stop from the token boundary 0.2 ms (L0) to 10.2 ms (L27); stop and re-entry bitwise; rerun bitwise; the attention replica rebuilt from the seam and the K/V arena equals the observed o_proj input exactly; K/V cell edits are a direct arena write: base margin -4.8048, effects A 3.519 / B 0.812 / A+B 4.873, interaction 0.542 (mdb on HF with re-rounded int8 weights: -4.8047, 3.517 / 0.812 / 4.871, 0.542). Kernel-vs-HF port differences on the real model (up to 1.3e-3 relative, logits 0.066) come from the weights, not the arithmetic: the store's int8 weights differ from a torch re-rounding of the checkpoint in 11k-584k elements per matrix, while store.matmul equals F.linear on the store's own weight bitwise. The int8 store is a different model from the bf16 checkpoint (margin -4.80 against -4.75; effects 3.52 / 0.81 / 4.87 against 3.75 / 1.0 / 5.125); no FP32 store of this model exists on beast. Not tested: batched kernel (batched_paged_logits), the CUDA decode graph, dense-qstore-cuda (fused SwiGLU and residual-norm kernels hide n/g/u/f), MLX, ANE, MoE kernels. mrun's `hf` backend already works unchanged (job-6470ef881011; needs attn_implementation='eager' and a dtype in model_kwargs).

detail: `verify` confirms a forecast when the measured residual is within N dtype spacings at the consumer's magnitude. N = 2 for a scalar target, N = 4 for a margin or a vector port. The 4 is asserted, not derived: it was chosen after the 28-layer tiny margin measured 2.7 spacings and two fp32 vector ports measured about 2.3 and 2.8 spacings at N = 2. A vector port's floor is taken at its largest element although elements round at their own magnitudes.
evidence: M29 agent report 2026-11-13 (commit ca331e6); analysis/forecast.py `verify` (`steps =`), analysis/verdict.py `confirm`

Print the residual in spacings so a near-floor pass is visible. Rerun on Qwen2.5-1.5B.
resolution: Closed in 30ce501: floor = 3 x sqrt(n) x dtype spacing at the consumer (a margin: the sum of both logits' spacings), n = rounded identities between seal and target (derived-exact count), judged per element; a finite sealed per-element bound tightens the floor at its element. The 3 is supplied: max measured residual/(sqrt(n) x spacing) over 12264 correct tiny qwen2/qwen3 forecasts (bf16/fp32, 2-28 layers) is 0.86 bf16 and 2.18 fp32 for vector ports, 1.91 and 1.80 for margins. The sqrt(n) growth is asserted (the data fit it as a conservative envelope). The old N=4 was too tight: correct margins measured 11-18 spacings. Spacing at each element's own magnitude is not usable (up to 1e4 own spacings on correct forecasts). `residual_spacings` is printed. Caveat: the sealed bound now decides where it tightens; a wrong bound premise could give a false `not confirmed` (0 violations in 1373 tiny cases). Not measured on a real model.

detail: `explain` of a margin is refused on any model with 32 or more layers: `result exceeds the record bound: explain result.explain.terms has 65 items (> 64); store it by pointer`. Two terms per layer plus the embedding. Same disease as M18 (forecast chain). Qwen2.5-1.5B (28 layers) is just under the limit.
evidence: job-d16ba4fd134b (SmolLM2-360M, 32 layers), M24 agent report 2026-11-13
next: Keep a bounded summary in the record (top terms by magnitude, the sum of the rest, the count) and store the full term list by pointer, as M18 did for the forecast chain. Sweep the other ops for lists that grow with layers or heads.
resolution: Closed in 61a54b6: explain of a margin keeps the 64 largest terms by |value| plus `terms_summary` (count, rest count and derived-exact sum, pointer); the full terms and per-layer rounding entries are a sha256-checked blob, in the project store with a project, in memory on the run without. Tiny qwen2 at 40 layers (70 for per_layer): result 28 KB, listed + rest + remainders equals the native margin. Sweep at 40 layers: reads, symbols, circuit, info, list, backtrace, compare ok; whatif refused (M40). Not run: 16-32 heads, a real 32-layer model, the web view.

detail: No port program for gemma or gemma2. gemma needs: RMSNorm gain (1 + w) through one norm_gain(module) helper used by every norm read in analysis/; the sqrt(d) embedding scale in the layer-0 h identity; a GELU-tanh activation column (value, first and second derivative, Lipschitz constant) in finite, forecast and propagate. gemma2 additionally: four norms per layer (new ports, a new rule for an r edit, margin decomposition through N(o)); attention-logit softcap and query_pre_attn_scalar in the s replica; the final-logit softcap (explain already refuses it).

detail: A port edit acts only on the cursor's row. Prompt rows are prefilled in one call and have no ports, so patching a port at an earlier prompt position (the usual position-by-layer activation patching sweep) has no direct form: it needs cache-cell edits for the prompt rows, which cover k/v only, not a head output, MLP output or residual at that position.
evidence: M28 agent report 2026-11-13; tests/test_ops_port_origin.py every-position test uses cache cells for rows 0-2
next: Either step the prompt row by row with forced tokens so every prompt row has ports (ties to M26), or add a row selector to port edits realised during prefill. Then a `sweep` over (row, layer, port) that returns one table of consumer deltas.
